pitch_detail.notes: Starts on a 5.6 ramp below the big left-facing chimney flake, then a short curving flake and a rightward move into a left-leaning dihedral. Finishes up and left over lichenous slab to the foot of the crack system. Runout (PG-13). A more direct line up a left-facing corner may exist.

Step right around a flake into a short splitter that eats cams from about 0.5 to 1. Follow broken cracks to a ledge sloping right, or go 15 feet farther to a comfortable stance beneath the lichen cracks.

Parallel lichen cracks lead to a right-leaning finger crack and then an easy chimney to a large ledge, where you can belay to skip rope stretch. Above the ledge a left-leaning crack goes to a pod, which is the crux. Exit the pod to another big belay ledge.
Easy ground up and over to join the north ridge route.

review.changed: 4 pitches written with stated grades and lengths (ft to m).

pitch_detail.notes: Short step past a chockstone, then deep snow to the first big chockstone. Can be soloed when the chockstone is mostly buried. Belay from a 0.5 cam in the left wall.

Chimney up under the chockstone, protecting where possible; a #4 cam helps. Pull the first roof to a stance by a squeeze chimney (a #1 fits), squeeze and stem past the chockstone, then tunnel through a large snow mushroom to an alcove. Belay from a slung pinch.

Strenuous chimneying leads under the next chockstones, where the first gear appears. The roof has been passed with a couple of aid points and very wild stemming. Another big snow mushroom needs tunnelling, then easy M4 stemming past a chockstone into a deep canyon. Wade steep snow to mid-canyon and belay on a knifeblade in the left wall, or climb higher and belay on screws, which exposes you to falling ice and rock from the next pitch.

Thin, steep ice leads to a flare choked with ice (WI5+) that needs offwidth technique to exit onto steep snow (M6/7 R). Continue through several rock bands (M5+, serious) separated by exposed steep snow for over 100 feet, then frozen turf to a small tree left of the obvious ice flow. About 250+ feet, the last 50+ simul-climbed; if you carry a drill and bolt kit, stopping after the flare is better.

Frozen turf, then a rightward traverse on mossy slab to the main ice flow, followed by about 100 feet of WI4 to a ledge below the last rock band. Belay on a 0.75 cam and a yellow C3. Runout, with poor protection.
Frozen turf and poor rock lead up and right, then fight past a pine to the snow above and wade up and left until the slope eases. Belay from a tree.

review.changed: 6 pitches written, grades as stated per pitch; P4 length given only as 250+ ft so left in notes. Descent not turned into a rappel table.

pitch_detail.notes: One long pitch up a narrow slot full of chockstones; difficulty swings a lot with snow cover. Awkward mixed slabbing past the last chockstone is the technical crux. Continue hard right at the top, then left to another chockstone.
Thin ice slab or mixed ground to get past the chockstone, then on to more ice on the right.
Steeper slab on the right gains the bench above; a longer low-angle flow just past it is an alternative. Continue left across the bench into the drainage and up to the pillar.

Belay at the bottom of the pillar or scramble easy ice to it and a small cave. The pillar is smaller than it looks from town (WI4, possibly a plus), then low-angle ice or sketchy mixed slab leads to a stump with tat. About 400 feet of snow follows to the next ice, possibly with a low-angle slab on the way.
A fat, pleasant flow, up and right to a tree with tat.
The last flow. A v-thread works best for the anchor.

review.changed: 6 pitches with stated lengths (m) and grades; P4 grade WI4 with a possible plus kept in notes. Descent is a rap list by pitch, not a station table, so no rappel_detail.

pitch_detail.notes: Kick steps up to a sheltered cave beneath the first chockstone. Climb the vertical wall right of centre inside the cave to the underside of the block, then traverse around the edge of the roof and exit onto ice. The grade is approximate; later in the season a pillar may form, possibly turning this into a WI4+ ice pitch with no drytooling.
Steep gully snow for a few hundred feet, suited to simul-climbing, to a second cave below another very large chockstone.

Chimney to the top at the back of the cave, then work out toward the chockstone and squeeze through a small gap behind it. One method is to lead through tied to the middle of the rope, clipping one strand only, then haul packs on the other strand. Anchor in the next cave roughly 20 feet higher, or extend the anchor down to the gap to ease hauling.
Leave the cave to the right and climb a last stretch of drytooling to the final snow slope.

review.changed: 4 pitches written; no lengths stated. Descent mentions a walk-off or rappels but no stations, so no rappel table.

pitch_detail.notes: Approximately M6. Starts on frozen turf, climbs a shallow corner, then moves out a small roof and traverses right about 30 feet. Protection is only fair.
Approximately M8. Climb up and right across a huge roof system and round a corner to a good belay cave. Physical tool torquing and laybacking; the gear is good.
Approximately M8. Finishes through the last chimney and roof on lichenous rock, with good gear. Several #2 to #4 cams cover the last two pitches.

review.changed: 3 pitches with stated lengths; grades are approximate and the route's grade is uncertain, flagged in notes.

pitch_detail.notes: Steep snow for about 300 feet, soloed or simul-climbed depending on conditions. Aim for the left side of the big cave under the chimney system.

Start left of the cave. A direct start right beside the chimney is thin, about M5 and poorly protected; starting around 20 feet farther left gives a safer tiered line. A square horn takes a girth hitch; step right across a narrow gap into the chimney and climb the moderate snow gully for about 150 feet. Belaying at the horn lets a 60 m rope reach a fixed pin and nut station with a red sling above the M4 wall; belaying lower on the snowfield stops about 40 feet short of it.
Steep but enjoyable climbing directly above the station with good protection, the ice offwidth. Continue up another moderate snow gully into the upper chimney and probably belay on the left.

Steep again, with good protection; the left side of the chimney is the choice. Head for the large chockstone that has daylight showing beneath it. The pitch finishes at the col behind Forbidden Tower's summit.
About 40 feet of rock to the summit, which is car-sized with big exposure. Take crampons off first, since the offwidth slot can trap a boot.

rappel_detail.anchor: sling with a locking carabiner at the summit
rappel_detail.notes: A full 60 m rappel lands about 30 feet above the pin and nut station; a purple sling around a boulder allows the short hop down to it.

rappel_detail.anchor: fixed pin and nut station with a red sling
rappel_detail.notes: A second 60 m rappel only just reaches the snowfield, and may not reach once the snow melts back. Glissade the slope to your stash if conditions allow.

review.changed: 5 pitches written (row stores 4). P1 is 300 ft of snow. Two summit rappels listed station by station.
review.other_findings: Stored pitches=4 but the description gives 5 pitches (P5 a short 5.6 summit bit).

pitch_detail.notes: About M7, the crux pitch. Climb the ice column, or drytool on fixed pins just left if the ice is poor. Above, a corner leads to a large precarious block, then seams and corners trending slightly right to a big sloping ledge with a fixed stopper anchor.
Several options exist. Traverse about 30 feet right, then trend up and right for roughly 150 feet to a grassy belay ledge. Approximately M5 to M6, runout on the opening traverse.

Options again. Go slightly right off the belay, then up and left to a short wide crack beneath a small roof, and hook through it to a huge snowy ledge. Approximately M5. From several spots on pitches 2 and 3 you can traverse right to join Brain Freeze.

review.changed: 3 pitches written (row stores 5). P2 length approximate so only in notes.
review.other_findings: Stored pitches=5, the description covers 3 pitches.

pitch_detail.notes: A double pillar or curtain. An anchor may already be on a small tree to the right at the top.
A shorter, easier pillar. An anchor may be in place on a small tree past a willow, on the right near the top.
Easy flow. Anchor options are scarce and most parties solo it. Then easy ramps and short flows up the creek; watch for deep pools below the drops.

A pillar or smear affected by sun, up to a chockstone, then easier ice leftward out of the main drainage and a shallow ramp to another short flow. Some accounts split this into two short pitches, but it links on 60 m ropes. Anchor possibly on thick willows to the right.
The big scenic flow, sustained WI4 with a good vertical stretch near the top. Anchor on screws or shrubs at the top.
Steep fat blue curtain, the steepness and technical crux. The easiest line is probably on the right. Anchor on screws or a stout little tree on the right.

rappel_detail.notes: Afterward, hike back down to the brink of the large pitch.
Afterward, hike down to the lip of the ice step below.
Reaches the creek bed below the chockstone. Ramble down the creek and downclimb toward P3, or traverse to a cluster of leaning trees west of the creek above the last step.
Rap first the short cliff that skirts the step, continuing the full way down P3 in one go. Hike to the next cliff and look for tree anchors.
Then walk out the way you came.

review.changed: 6 pitches with stated grades/lengths; rappel table built from the descent list in order (6 stations).

pitch_detail.notes: From the big grassy ledge about 40 feet left of Warhead, zig-zag up slabby terrain with scattered cracks, runout (PG-13), then blocky ground to a sloping ledge under a shallow left-leaning corner.

Up the shallow left-leaning corner to its top, then 5.10+ slab moves to an undercling. Pull small roofs, traverse right on a ledge and through another bulge to a long sloping ledge that widens into a ramp. Belay where gear allows, about halfway up the ramp.
Jam 5.8 cracks along the ramp face to a dihedral that faces left, and stop beneath the steeper pair of cracks to its left.

Take the right-hand crack (5.9) until it gets steeper and drifts left. Set a high piece, then downclimb and traverse right and make 5.10- moves to reach a crack in a shallow groove, which runs to a big ledge. A fifth pitch exists: go left for the final pitch of Lost Arrowhead (5.10b) or right for Warhead (5.9).

review.changed: 4 pitches written (P1-P4); P5 is a finish on neighbouring routes so noted in P4. Descent mentions 2 rappels without stations: no table.
review.other_findings: Description lists 5 pitches (P5 is a finish up Lost Arrowhead or Warhead); stored 4.

pitch_detail.notes: Start up a broken slab and crack, then step left to a left-trending left-facing dihedral. Reach parallel cracks, follow them to a second left-facing dihedral, and climb it or the crack on its left until it forms a narrow sloping ledge, where you belay.

Climb the face (two crux moves) to a hanging left-facing dihedral, up it to the roof, then traverse left beneath the roof and up to the ramp. Thin, finicky protection in the lower dihedral justifies the PG-13 rating.

review.changed: 2 pitches, no lengths or per-pitch grades stated.

pitch_detail.notes: Start in ledgy ground just left of Manic Laughter below a corner with a hand crack and fist-size section. Climb the corner at 5.9+, or the right-hand of two face finger cracks at 5.11-, which protects well.

Twin finger cracks in the left face would probably go near 5.12-, but flaky rock and so-so starting gear make the hand crack up the corner the usual choice. Belay at Ledge 2, then continue by another line or rappel.

review.changed: 2 pitches with stated lengths; P1 grade alternatives kept in notes. Route ends at Ledge 2; rappel via slung blocks on a neighbouring route, not a station list.

pitch_detail.notes: Pick a way through blocky terrain to the left end of the traverse ledge, belaying in a small nook, or start farther right toward the middle. Pitch length is 45 m or 60 m depending on where you start. A 70 m rope links this with the next pitch using long runners.
Traverse the ledge carefully past big loose blocks to its right end. Build the belay a metre or two before the next moves so the start of P3 avoids weak rock.

In the big corner take the clean smaller left-facing corner, jamming and laybacking to a roof. The original line goes left through a thin finger crack. The Wendy's Way alternative exits the roof on the right: stem, reach right to a little horn at the roof's lower right corner, cut feet and swing right to a hand hold or jug, then follow a sinuous crack to a belay ledge.
A wide crack into a corner, then jam or layback and stem to a more vertical headwall. Thin cracks with horizontals lead to the summit; watch for loose rock at the lip.

review.changed: 4 pitches written, grades/lengths as stated; P1 length is a range (45 or 60 m) given in notes. No rappels listed.
review.other_findings: P3 is graded 5.10 in the description while the stored route grade is 5.9.

pitch_detail.notes: Start on the obvious arete on the big ledge below Zeb's Arete. Delicate face climbing with thin moves; the crux comes about 30 feet up, with solid passive gear in thin cracks. It eases below a blank slab: use the flared pod, move right and up the slab runout, and belay below the dihedral. Runout (R).
From under the left-facing dihedral, sweet jams until it pinches. After the ledge, a chimney with loose flakes leads to a big ledge among boulders where you belay.
Optional pitch, exposed, with limited gear along the upper ridgeline. Stay on the southeast side for about 40 m. Then 300 feet of 4th and 5th class scrambling along ledges reaches the top.

review.changed: 3 pitches written; no lengths stated. P3 optional 5th class.

pitch_detail.notes: East-facing. Start in a right-facing splitter for 25 feet, then right along a foot ramp and up a broken crack system to a ramp under the roof crux. Clip the bolt before the awkward moves over the arete, then traverse left on a sloping ledge, clipping a second bolt at a bulge. The bolts keep the rope off the arete.
Tight hands that shrink to ring locks in a dihedral facing left lead to a lobe of rock. After that three bolts protect easier and easier ground.

review.changed: 2 pitches with stated grades, lengths and bolts where given.

pitch_detail.notes: Climb the opening pitch of Walk On The Wild Side to its hanging belay.

An overhanging finger-and-hand crack (5.10) takes you over the first roof, and a belay just left is possible. The second roof looks like a burly wide crack: medium gear fits deep inside, or bear hug the right-hand arete (5.11a) and get back in the crack at the lip. Keep going to a ledge roughly 165 feet above the base.
Easy, lower-angle terrain to a ledge.

A fine 60-foot finger crack (5.9+ or 5.10a), then a chimney up to the north summit. Descend by a short rappel or downclimb of the chimney at the summit's south end, to the terrace beneath the south spire and the top of the descent chimney.

review.changed: 4 pitches written; P1 is the first pitch of Walk On The Wild Side, no lengths except P4's.

pitch_detail.notes: The first pitch of Good Evans, belaying on top of the flake. The belay takes hand-size pieces.
Climb 10 to 15 feet of the Good Evans crack to a good rail, traverse left, then follow a tips-to-fingers crack up into the roof of Cary Granite and past it. The traverse is probably about 5.9.
Climb to the top.

Begin on the featured ground just right of the dihedral and chimney section, aiming for a small dihedral facing right, about 25 feet up and left of a wide black groove. Climb slab to a small ledge tucked behind a big block, go right and up, then angle left into the main dihedral and a ledge with a #3 cam slot above. Expect rope drag.
Cross right a short way and go up before reaching a tree, angling right up the dihedral or the slab beside it. Belay in the chimney or link into the next section.
Work up the chimney, with optional big-cam slots. Rope drag out of the chimney calls for a belay, with a perfect #11 hex and a small Alien slot.

Exposed dihedral and perhaps the crux moves. Move right below a big block and jam the crack, stemming out on the left, then briefly use the left crack and come back right to a stance. A large ledge follows, with a precarious block hanging from it. About 120 feet; the next pitch can be linked.

Chimney facing right up a large slot; many moves are possible without hands, and beware of gear hanging off your back. Small protection plus a #4 cam. Another loose block sits right and below the chockstone. Belay in a small stand of trees; length 40 to 120 feet depending on the tree.

pitch_detail.notes: Easy right-facing corner to a ledge, then easy ground to the foot of a left-facing dihedral.
A dihedral leads to a tree ledge; belay at the ledge's left side.
Leave straight up from the ledge's left end through a shallow corner and over a small roof, then climb the face to a stance under an overhang. Runout.
Pass over the overhang and continue to a larger overhang.
Get past the roof at its side and continue to a belay ledge above.
Face between two opposing corners up to a big grassy ledge.
Fifth-class terrain to the summit.
